title: Annotatio V §.VIII reply (2): vivification/solace only for spiritual eaters — stop §.VIII before §.IX
pass_a_gloss: (2) While vivification and purgation from the filth of sins, and thence the juice of solace arising from these for those eating either and drinking, is ascribed to Christ’s flesh and blood present either outside the Sacred Supper or in the Supper itself, it will certainly be judged to be ascribed to no other eaters and drinkers than those eating and drinking Spiritually — the rest who eat and drink also apart from Spiritual eating and drinking being altogether without all solace, much less this juice. So that it may be understood most clearly that the juice of solace flows not from the Oral Eating of Christ’s body but from the Spiritual, and that not those eating oraliter but those finally eating spiritualiter can cry within themselves with Monica from the too-great joy of their spiritual soul: Let us fly away, Let us fly away. Or rather with the whole Company of the pious and those worthily communicating with Christ, thunder for joy at Isaiah ch. 61: I altogether rejoice in Jehovah. Namely: After I was commanded to eat, I hearkened to the Lord, and I ate the good, and my soul was delighted. Isa. 55:2, collated with 1 Cor. 10:3–4.
pass_b_english: Reply (2): vivification, purgation, and solace-juice belong only to those who eat and drink spiritually — others who eat without spiritual eating have no solace at all.

So the juice flows from Spiritual eating, not Oral. Only spiritual eaters can cry Evolemus with Monica — or with Isaiah’s company rejoice in Jehovah after eating the good (Isa. 55:2; 1 Cor. 10:3–4). Stop §.VIII before §.IX.
source_text: (2) Dum carni & sanguini Christi, vel extra Cœnam S., vel in ipsâ Cœna, præsentibus, vivificatio & à sordibus peccatorum purgatio indeque manducantibus utrumque, & bibentibus solatii succus, ab istis oriundus, transscribitur, non aliis certè manducantibus ac bibentibus transscribendus censebitur, quàm Spiritualiter manducantibus & bibentibus, reliquis & citra manducationem & bibitionem Spiritualem manducantibus & bibentibus, omnis solatii, nedum succi hujus, expertibus omnino. Ut sic clarissimè intelligatur, succum solatii non ex Manducatione corporis Christi Orali, sed Spirituali profluere, neque oraliter, sed spiritualiter demum manducantes, præ nimio gaudio animi sui spiritualis, intra se, cum Monica, exclamare posse: Evolemus Evolemus. Vel cum integro potiùs piorum & dignè Christo communicantium Cœtu, apud Esaiam cap. 61. præ gaudio intonare: Omnino gaudeo in Jehova. Sc. Postquam jussus edere, auscultavi Domino, & comedi bonum & oblectata est anima mea. Esa. 55, 2. coll. cum 1. Cor. 10, 3. 4.

lemmas.gloss: juice of solace … flows from the Spiritual
